overview: State Representative Christine Barber, a candidate for the Second Middlesex District State Senate seat, appeared on Medford Happenings to discuss her legislative record and priorities. The conversation focused on housing affordability, economic development, government transparency, and infrastructure projects in Medford.

items.title: Candidate Introduction and Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced State Representative Christine Barber, who discussed her decade of experience in the legislature and her background as a healthcare advocate and community organizer.

items.title: Cost of Living and Housing Policy
items.summary: Barber addressed the affordability crisis by highlighting her work on foreclosure prevention programs, accessory dwelling unit legislation, and laws to eliminate co-pays for chronic illness medications.

items.title: Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act (TOPA)
items.summary: Barber detailed her support for TOPA legislation, which would grant tenants a right of first refusal to collectively purchase their buildings at market rate to prevent displacement by developers.

items.title: District Engagement and Community Outreach
items.summary: Barber described her strategy for connecting with the diverse populations of Medford, Somerville, Cambridge, and Winchester through direct door-knocking and attending local senior and cultural events.

items.title: Economic Development and Revenue Streams
items.summary: The discussion covered efforts to expand the commercial tax base, including a proposed tax on online retailers to fund downtown improvements and state support for clean energy businesses on Mystic Avenue.

items.title: Vocational Education and Workforce Training
items.summary: Barber emphasized the importance of state funding for vocational and technical programs at Medford High School to prepare students for the local workforce.

items.title: Legislative Transparency and Recorded Votes
items.summary: Barber advocated for greater transparency on Beacon Hill, noting she has pushed to make committee votes public and easily accessible to voters online.

items.title: State Grant Tracking and Infrastructure Projects
items.summary: Barber addressed the challenges of multi-agency project timelines, specifically discussing the status of a million-dollar grant for the Main Street and South Street intersection and funding for the Mystic Community Market.

items.title: Legislative Audit Response
items.summary: Barber expressed her support for auditing the state legislature and noted her vote to codify the annual disclosure of legislative financial records into state law.
